 Updated Tue, Oct 20 2026 4:13 PM EDT Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow jumps 500 points as earnings optimism steadies market: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Lee Ying Shan Fred Imbert A trader works at the New York Stock Exchange on Oct. 20, 2026. NYSE The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose on Tuesday as a number of upbeat earnings reports and a drop in oil prices overshadowed recent pressure seen among artificial intelligence-related stocks.
 The blue-chip index gained 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to end at 52,495.88, while the S&P 500 added 0.28% and closed at 7,712.57. The Nasdaq Composite inched down 0.02% to 26,424.82.
 Shares of industrial and safety products producer 3M offered a boost to the Dow, jumping more than 5% following better-than-expected earnings results and a full-year guidance raise . Shares of aerospace and defense company Northrop Grumman advanced more than 4% after it posted an earnings beat.
 Meanwhile, oil prices pulled back from earlier gains, helping investor sentiment. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 1.8% to settle at $101.79, while Brent crude futures declined 0.7% to $108.79 a barrel. The moves in oil, which added to the declines in Treasury yields , come as traders continued to monitor developments in the Middle East.
 The market has been weighed down as of late by worries about the sustainability of the AI trade amid debt and demand concerns. In fact, sentiment in tech took a hit earlier in the day after Korean AI firm Elice tumbled more than 30% overnight in its public market debut. Asia-Pacific markets declined Tuesday, after U.S. stocks rose overnight, leading to declines in the South Korean market.
 However, some AI-related stocks staged a bit of a comeback as the session went on. Western Digital gained more than 3%, while Seagate Technology was up more than 2%. CoreWeave and Marvell Technology each advanced more than 1%.
 The S&P 500 finished in positive territory on Monday, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced more than 1%. That marked a rebound from last week's rout, when anxieties around companies borrowing too much money for their AI build-outs intensified.
 "For much of this year, the market has been willing to look through higher rates because the growth story, notably that around AI, was strong enough to justify it. Last week, we saw that relationship begin to be tested," said Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion.
 "Hyperscalers report over the next few weeks, setting up the next major stress test for the AI trade," he continued. "Guidance around ROI, data center spending and 2027 capex will arguably be more important than the headline earnings figures."
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 4:12 PM EDT Dow, S&P 500 finish higher
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 ended Tuesday's session with gains.
 The 30-stock index added 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, while the broad market index rose 0.28% to 7,712.57.
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq closed just below the flatline, however, dropping 0.02% to 26,424.82.
 — Sean Conlon 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 3:21 PM EDT S&P 500 sees broad support
 The S&P 500 was up 0.3% in afternoon trading on Tuesday, and the index's gains were bolstered by various parts of the market.
 As of 3:20 p.m. ET, the index had 414 gainers and only 89 laggards.
 Eight of the index's 11 sectors were also in positive territory, with health care, real estate and utilities leading the charge. Health care was up more than 2%, while real estate and utilities were each higher by nearly 2% and more than 1%, respectively. 
 Communication services, information technology and energy were the three sectors seeing losses on the day.
 — Sean Conlon 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 2:34 PM EDT Netflix shares fall ahead of earnings
 Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Shares of Netflix were down more than 1% in afternoon trading on Tuesday as investors geared up for the release of its latest quarterly results after the bell.
 Analysts surveyed by LSEG are expecting the company to report 82 cents in earnings per share and revenue of $12.87 billion.
 The report comes amid a downbeat year for the stock, as it's fallen more than 26%.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon NFLX, year-to-date — Sean Conlon and Sarah Whitten 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 1:18 PM EDT Activist CEO says value stocks are poised to benefit from using AI
 Jeff Smith, chief executive officer of Starboard Value LP, speaks during a Bloomberg Television interview in New York, U.S. Christopher Goodney | Bloomberg | Getty Images Starboard Value CEO, Jeff Smith believes the coming years "is going to be amazing," for value stocks, he told CNBC at the 13D Monitor Active-Passive Investor Summit Tuesday. 
 It's because companies that use artificial intelligence across their organizations should improve their margins "much faster" from creating greater efficiencies.  
 His comments come as he sees many value stocks currently trading at low multiples. 
 "Being able to buy in at that value and be your own catalyst to get them to improve their margins; I think the next, how ever many years, is going to be amazing," Smith said.
 — Paulina Likos 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 12:41 PM EDT Stocks making big moves: Hasbro, Equifax, Dream Finders Homes
 Check out the companies making the biggest moves midday: 
 Hasbro — Shares gained more than 5% after the toymaker reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. Hasbro also raised its revenue growth outlook for the full year.
 Equifax – Shares of the consumer credit bureau leapt almost 12%. Equifax earned $2.26 per share on an adjusted basis in the third quarter, beating the FactSet consensus of $2.20. Revenue of $1.69 billion was in line with expectations. The company dialed back its revenue guidance for 2026, however.
 Dream Finders Homes — The homebuilder rose more than 8% after it completed the acquisition of Beazer Homes that was announced Aug. 7.
 Read here for the full list.
 — Sarah Min 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 12:10 PM EDT TD Cowen upgrades BlackRock to buy from hold 
 A sign is posted on the exterior of a BlackRock office on Jan. 15, 2026 in San Francisco, California. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images TD Cowen upgraded BlackRock to buy from hold on Tuesday, citing the company is ahead of revenue and operating income targets. 
 TD Cowen's Bill Katz also increased the company's price target to $1,405, a nearly 25% upside from Monday's close. 
 Katz added that BlackRock has several avenues for organic growth, including in private markets and retirement. 
 — Ananya Chetia 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 11:21 AM EDT 3M shares pop after earnings 
 3M shares popped more than 5% after the producer of industrial and safety products posted adjusted earnings of $2.50 per share, more than the LSEG estimate of $2.38 per share.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon 3M, 1-day — Sarah Min 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 10:55 AM EDT GE Aerospace slips after earnings 
 Military officials and visitors from various countries tour the GE Aerospace booth during the Seoul International Aerospace and Defense Exhibition (ADEX 2025) at KINTEX in Ilsan, Goyang, South Korea, on October 20, 2025. Chris Jung | Nurphoto | Getty Images Shares of GE Aerospace were off 2% after the company reported its third-quarter financials, where the company delivered an earnings and revenue beat. 
 GE Aerospace reported adjusted earnings of $2.25 per share, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's estimates for $2.01 per share. Revenue also came in above expectations at $13.29 billion. 
 The company also hiked guidance across various metrics for the full-year, however free cash flow at $2.04 billion was lower than expectations for $2.2 billion, according to StreetAccount. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon GE Aerospace three-month. — Davis Giangiulio 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 9:35 AM EDT S&P 500, Nasdaq opens lower
 The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite began Tuesday's session in the red.
 The broad market index fell 0.2% just after 9:30 a.m. ET, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq pulled back 0.4%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average traded around the flatline.
 — Sean Conlon 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 9:03 AM EDT CoreWeave credit seeing more signs of stress
 Thomas Fuller | Lightrocket | Getty Images Investor concerns over CoreWeave 's credit ticked higher on Tuesday, with the spread on its five-year credit default swap rising back up near levels seen on Thursday . 
 The CDS, which is a way for buyers to pay for protection in case the borrower defaults, last saw spreads over 1,121, which is up 2.22% for the day and more than 17% over the past week. Spreads of 1,000 or greater are generally considered a sign of distress.
 CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps on Oct. 20, 2026 — Michelle Fox 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 8:44 AM EDT Housing starts tumble in September as real estate woes continue
 Construction workers rebuild a home in the Eaton Fire burn zone on March 6, 2026 in Altadena, California. Mario Tama | Getty Images Housing starts slumped in September, raising fresh concerns about the state of the real estate market as the Federal Reserve contemplates additional interest rate hikes.
 The Commerce Department reported Tuesday that privately owned starts totaled 1.22 million at a seasonally adjusted annualized rate. That was off 5.2% from the August level and well below the Dow Jones consensus for 1.3 million.
 Additionally, single-family starts weakened, totaling 859,000, off 4.6% from the prior month.
 Building permits issued during the month were slightly better than expected, totaling a seasonally adjusted annualized 1.4 million, against the estimate for 1.39 million. The total was 0.2% below August.
 — Jeff Cox 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 8:11 AM EDT RTX, Northrop Grumman and Steel Dynamics among the stocks making premarket moves
 Check out the companies making headlines before the bell: 
 RTX — The defense stock rose after RTX posted adjusted earnings of $1.80 per share in the third quarter on revenue of $24.97 billion. That surpassed the LSEG consensus estimate of $1.78 per share and $24.08 billion.
 Northrop Grumman — Shares gained 0.5% after the defense contractor reported mixed results for the third quarter. The company earned $7.89 per share, beating an LSEG estimate of $7.18 per share. However, revenue of $11.12 billion was just below the $11.14 billion consensus.
 Steel Dynamics — Shares dropped 5.3% after the industrial metals company reported mixed third-quarter numbers. While the company beat on revenue, its earnings per share and profit margin fell short of expectations. On a positive note, the company's customer backlog is up 50% year over year, extending into 2027 as strong demand persists.
 Read here for the full list.
 — Sarah Min 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 7:57 AM EDT General Motors shares fall after latest quarterly results
 The GM logo is displayed at the new location of the General Motors Headquarters in Detroit, Michigan, U.S., January 12, 2026. Rebecca Cook | Reuters General Motors beat Wall Street's expectations on the top- and bottom-lines as it reported its Q3 2026 earnings, delivering strong results driven by high truck sales and growing subscription revenue 
 The company raised its free cash flow expectations and narrowed its 2026 full-year guidance.
 The Detroit automaker also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion, but didn't provide a specific timeframe for the repurchase.
 "GM is performing well, and we are working hard to continue our momentum despite growing inflationary pressures through strategic investments in new products and services, and through improved quality and operating efficiency," GM CEO Mary Barra said Tuesday in a letter to shareholders. 
 GM expects commodity inflation costs to be nearly $2 billion, which was the high end of its previous guidance. The automaker also said the costs of its pullback in all-electric vehicles announced last year were "substantially completed."
 GM stock was off roughly 7% during premarket trading despite the beats. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon General Motors stock price year-to-date — Deena Zaidi 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 7:44 AM EDT Elice tumbles 30% in Korean market debut
 Korean AI firm Elice tumbled more than 30% overnight in its public market debut. Investors recently have been worried about the sustainability of the AI trade, as debt and demand concerns grow .
 — Fred Imbert 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 6:31 AM EDT Solstice rises on report of Starboard Value stake
 Shares of Solstice Advanced Materials , which was spun off from Honeywell last year, rose more than 3% after The Financial Times reported, citing sources, that activist Starboard Value had built a stake in the company. 
 Starboard wants Solstice to cut about $100 million in corporate costs focus on its refrigerants and nuclear businesses, the report said . Solstice shares are up more than 24% year to date. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon SOLS in 2026 — Fred Imbert 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 6:22 AM EDT Northrop Grumman rises on earnings beat
 Northrop Grumman gained more than 1% after the defense contractor reported mixed results for the third quarter. 
 The company earned $7.89 per barrel, beating an LSEG estimate of $7.18 per share. However, revenue of $11.12 billion was just below the $11.14 billion consensus.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon NOC 5-day chart Tue, Oct 20 2026 4:22 AM EDT ABB CEO sees no slowdown in data center demand despite investor concerns
 Morten Wierod, chief executive officer of ABB Ltd., speaks during the China Development Forum in Beijing, China, on Sunday, March 22, 2026. Qilai Shen | Bloomberg | Getty Images ABB CEO Morten Wierod told CNBC he sees no slowdown in the AI data center buildout in the coming years, despite investors becoming wary of ballooning AI spend . 
 The Swiss multinational firm declined around 6% on Tuesday, even after reporting record third-quarter orders , which jumped 40% to $12 billion, driven by a triple-digit increase in its data center segment. 
 "ABB without data centers, it is a double-digit growth when you look at the order intake," Wierod told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe." 
 "I believe there is a strong trend...you will see a continued build-out of the data center capacity in the coming years," Wierod added. 
 watch now VIDEO 3:34 03:34 ABB CEO: Where there is electricity, there will be data center build out Squawk Box Europe Other data center stocks were also down Tuesday. Schneider Electric and Siemens Energy fell 3% and 4%, respectively. Meanwhile, neocloud companies Coreweave and Nebius were both down around 3% in premarket trading.
 — Sawdah Bhaimiya 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 4:16 AM EDT South Koreas' Kospi leads losses as Asia markets fall
 Asia-Pacific markets closed in the red on Tuesday, with South Korean equities leading the losses.
 The Kospi dropped 3.73% to end the day at 5,552.74. Index heavyweight SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics are down 4.23% and 2.98% respectively. The small-cap Kosdaq index fell more than 3% at 781.97.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 declined 1.3% to 64,075.42, while the Topix slid 1.43% to 4,009.21. 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.33% to 8,816.9.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 3:32 AM EDT European stocks open lower as tech stocks fall
 The pan-European Stoxx 600 was 0.3% lower in early trading, dragged down by losses in the tech sector. 
 By 8:25 a.m. in London (3:25 a.m. ET), the Stoxx Europe 600 Technology index was down by 1.4%. 
 Chip stocks fell, with ASML down 2.5%, ASMI down 3.3% and BE Semiconductor down 3.6%. 
 Tuesday's moves marked the second consecutive day of broad losses in Europe, with the Stoxx 600 shedding 0.8% on Monday to snap a three-day winning streak. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 2:09 AM EDT UK wages grow faster than expected ahead of Bank of England interest rates decision 
 U.K. wages excluding bonuses grew by 3.7% year-on-year in the three months to August, official data showed on Tuesday, narrowly beating the 3.6% forecast by economists polled by Reuters. 
 The Office for National Statistics data comes ahead of an expected interest rate hike from the Bank of England next month.
 The bank, which is set to hike its "base rate" by 25 basis points to 4%, is concerned that the Iran war energy price shock is driving broader inflation, including via wages. 
 BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said last week the longer the war goes on, the harder it will be for the BoE not to respond. But he also said it remains "early days" and inflation pressures remained "quite subdued."
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 2:00 AM EDT French stocks head for further declines after turmoil
 A view of fire as streets across Paris show signs of damage following a day of violent clashes between police and protesters amid a nationwide mobilization over rising living costs, fuel prices, and education funding in Paris, France, on October 18, 2026. Ibrahim Ezzat | Anadolu | Getty Images France's CAC 40 index is set to open lower on Tuesday, according to IG futures data, following a 1.1% decline on Monday. 
 The country's stock market has severely lagged its European peers this year amid political volatility and social unrest over the cost of living and other issues, which boiled over into mass protests over the weekend . 
 Analysts told CNBC on Monday that French stocks were being harmed by higher government bond yields and the country's widening spread over Germany, along with a downturn in luxury spending. 
 The U.K.'s FTSE 100 , Germany's DAX and Italy's MIB were also seen opening in the red. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon France CAC 40 index. — Jenni Reid 
 Tue, Oct 20 2026 12:14 AM EDT Oil prices inch higher on Middle East worries
 Oil prices rose Tuesday as Iran-backed Houthis escalate attacks against Saudi Arabia, raising concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East.
 Brent crude futures rose 0.14% to $109.70 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures for November delivery gained 0.25% to $103.92 per barrel.
 The Houthis claimed on Monday to have attacked King Khalid International Airport again; Abha International Airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia, close to Yemen; Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu on the Red Sea Coast; the Shaybah oilfield and Saudi naval forces.
 Prospects of more Russian supplies hitting the market, however, kept a lid on prices.
 U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday waived several Russia-related sanctions, allowing countries such as India to purchase energy from Moscow.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 Mon, Oct 19 2026 11:27 PM EDT BlackRock, GIC chase Indian telecom major Jio's IPO as anchor bids top $26 billion
 India's Jio Platforms has seen the anchor investor quota for its initial public offering oversubscribed more than 30 times, according to a source familiar with the matter, drawing bids from top asset managers including BlackRock, Capital Group and GIC. 
 The country's largest telecommunications and digital services company, backed by Meta and Google, plans to raise up to 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) through India's largest ever IPO in rupee terms .
 According to the source, who is not allowed to speak on the matter due to legal restrictions, the company's anchor book received total bids worth 2.5 trillion rupees ($26.3 billion) for the 81.1 billion rupee anchor book portion.
 Jio Platforms in a release on Monday said it had finalized the allocation of 72.47 million equity shares to anchor investors at 1,119 rupees a share, at the upper range of the price band. 
 The anchor book is a portion of the total fundraise set aside for large institutional investors before the IPO opens for public bidding. 
 — Priyanka Salve 
 Mon, Oct 19 2026 10:48 PM EDT Indonesia's benchmark Jakarta Composite rebounds 3%
 Indonesia's benchmark Jakarta Composite Index rebounded 3% on Tuesday after the country's stock exchange announced plans to remove companies with highly concentrated ownership from the index.
 The move comes as authorities seek to address concerns raised by global index provider MSCI, and follow the index's plunged to a six-year low in the previous session.
 Indonesia seeks to avert a potential downgrade by MSCI to "standalone market" status, a classification reserved for markets that fall short of the accessibility, size or liquidity requirements of its broader indexes.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 Mon, Oct 19 2026 8:58 PM EDT Asian chip stocks slide as AI spending fears linger
 Asian chip stocks fell Tuesday, bucking an overnight rebound in U.S. technology shares as concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending continued to weigh on sentiment.
 South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix slid 4.07%, while Samsung Electronics lost 1.03%. 
 In Japan, tech investor SoftBank Group tumbled 4.46%, while chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron shed 1.45% and Renesas Electronics fell 1.49%. 
 The declines come as the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rebounded more than 1% on Monday, with U.S. chip giant Nvidia gaining 1.4%, Intel advancing 2%, Advanced Micro Devices and Micron adding adding 1.8% and about 3%, respectively.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 Mon, Oct 19 2026 8:09 PM EDT Japan's Nikkei 225 and South Korea's Kospi slide 
 Asia-Pacific markets opened in the red on Tuesday.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 declined 0.85%, while the Topix slid 0.56%. South Korea's Kospi lost 2.20%, while the small-cap Kosdaq was down 1.03%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 traded 0.84% lower.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 Mon, Oct 19 2026 7:42 PM EDT Asia-Pacific markets set to open subdued
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to fall Tuesday, breaking ranks with Wall Street that rose as U.S. technology stocks rebounded from last week's sharp sell-off.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  was poised to decline at open, with its Chicago futures contract last at 64,910, compared with the index's previous close of 64,916.7.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index stood at 24,112 lower than the index's last close of 24,186.83.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.9% in early trade.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 Mon, Oct 19 2026 6:12 PM EDT Stocks are ready to move on from the AI rout. The credit market is not
 AI stocks rallied on Monday, but CoreWeave closed slightly lower as investors remained skittish about its debt. Yields on Oracle debt also remained elevated as credit worries persist across the AI trade.
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 1% on Monday. CoreWeave , the so-called neocloud company that led the sell-off last week, bounced around, hit a 52-week low and ultimately closed fractionally lower. Meanwhile, its bond yields remained high and its five-year credit default swaps were at distressed levels.
 Read more here. 
 — Michelle Fox 
 Mon, Oct 19 2026 6:04 PM EDT Stock futures open higher
 Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded 56 points higher, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.1%. Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.2%.
 — Fred Imbert
